Scale mismatch can make a narrow residual-coefficient grid ineffective: dot products depend on embedding norms, whereas cosine scores are bounded; measure each branch’s candidate-score standard deviation and top-10 boundary margins per category ([Google](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/recommendation/overview/candidate-generation)). Practical fusion controls: independently standardize branches with an epsilon floor, then blend; use min–max normalization ([Elastic documentation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/retrievers/linear-retriever)); or reciprocal-rank fusion to remove score-scale dependence ([Cormack et al.](https://cormack.uwaterloo.ca/cormacksigir09-rrf.pdf)). Temperature scaling provides another scalar adjustment ([Guo et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599)); mathematically, dividing one branch by temperature before additive fusion is equivalent to changing its coefficient. It therefore adds no expressive power beyond a sufficiently broad coefficient search. These are transferable fusion methods, not evidence that this particular SASRec residual improves HR@10.

For history weighting, [ANIIP](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8802775/) directly studies exponentially attenuated item–item contributions and a complementary normalized branch; it does not establish the exact requested three-way cosine-residual comparison. An inexpensive proposed ablation freezes one trained SASRec checkpoint and its learned item embeddings, then compares SASRec alone, similarity alone, and fusion using last-item-only, uniform last-K history, and exponential last-K history. Compute r(i)=Σ w_t cos(e_t,e_i)/Σ w_t, excluding padding; use identical K, score normalization, and coefficient grids. Uniform versus exponential isolates recency; last-item-only tests whether older history helps. Include coefficient zero and several decay rates. Cache branch scores and select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Keep normalization consistent between sampled validation candidates and full-catalog recommendations; candidate-dependent normalization can change the effective blend.
